documents.title: NOVA Policies and Procedures syllabus insert, Fall 2026
documents.stance_why: Coder A coded restrict, coder B delegates. The source says AI use "to complete assigned work may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy" and urges caution with assignment web tools without "their instructors' explicit permission". There are no tiers or instructor-choice menu; the default is that AI to complete work is presumptively misconduct unless an instructor permits it. That matches restrict (banned unless explicitly permitted), though hedged with 'may'; delegates is not chosen because the document states a default rather than only handing the decision over.
documents.summary: A one-paragraph academic integrity section in the Fall 2026 NOVA Online syllabus insert. It says AI use to complete assigned work may violate the academic integrity policy, urges caution with assignment-assist web tools without instructor permission, and lists penalties. It sets no AI rule of its own beyond that.

units.why: The sentence says "the use of AI to complete assigned work may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy". It classes AI use on assignments as potential academic misconduct, so P36; it is hedged ('may'), hence informs, and it binds students.
units.anchor: use of AI to complete assigned work may be considered a violation
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, type P36 and unit_stance restrict; they differed on modality (A informs, B should-not). The source says AI use 'may be considered a violation', which reports a possible classification rather than directing students, so informs is kept. Topics follow the codebook list (A's 'enforcement'/'prohibited' are not valid codes).

units.why: "Students are urged to be cautious when using any web tools designed to assist with assignments without their instructors' explicit permission" advises care and ties use to instructor permission. It does not ban, so it is closest to P03 (discourage without forbidding); P04 is not chosen because no per-instructor decision procedure is set.
units.anchor: Students are urged to be cautious when using any web tools designed to assist
units.fit_note: Also makes instructors' explicit permission the condition for using such web tools; it does not name AI explicitly.
units.resolution_why: A coded P03 (discourage without forbidding), B coded P06 (fallback when syllabus silent). The source urges students to be 'cautious' with assignment-assist tools absent instructors' explicit permission; it does not say what applies when a syllabus is silent, it advises care. P03 fits better; P06 requires a firm fallback rule. Actor, phase, modality (should) and unit_stance agreed.

units.why: "cite their sources in all their work" is a general citation duty attached to the AI/web tool sentence. It is nearest to P24 (acknowledge or cite use), though it does not name AI or a statement.
units.anchor: to cite their sources in all their work
units.fit_note: Generic citation of sources; AI is not named, and no format or statement is specified.
units.resolution_why: Type, actor, phase and modality agreed (P24, student, during-work, should). Unit_stance differed (A permit, B neutral); a generic duty to cite sources neither permits nor restricts AI, so neutral.

units.why: "Consequences of academic dishonesty can include a failing grade on an assignment, a failing grade in the course" lists concrete sanctions for academic dishonesty, which the document extends to AI use; so P37, though the penalties are 'can include', not fixed.
units.anchor: a failing grade on an assignment, a failing grade in the course
units.frag_end: suspension or expulsion from the college.
units.fit_note: Penalties are for academic dishonesty generally, not AI specifically.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and type; only topic labels differed, and the codebook labels were used.

units.why: "NOVA faculty may choose to use tools such as Turnitin to detect and flag instances of plagiarism" permits faculty to use similarity-checking software; P40 covers similarity checking. AI detection is not named.
units.anchor: NOVA faculty may choose to use tools such as Turnitin to detect and flag
units.fit_note: Names plagiarism detection only, not AI detection.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and type; only topic labels differed, and the codebook labels were used.

notes: Only one sentence concerns AI explicitly; other units are the surrounding integrity text it relies on. Academic Integrity Policy 224 not read. Spring 2026 insert excluded as superseded. Reconciled: A and B matched on all 5 units; differences were document stance, one modality, one policy_type, one unit_stance, and topic labels.
